discovery: Semiconductor quantum-dot sources of single photons on demand

nominees.name: Pascale Senellart
nominees.affiliation: Centre for Nanosciences and Nanotechnology (C2N), CNRS / Université Paris-Saclay, France

motivation: In 2000, Michler, İmamoğlu and co-workers showed that a single semiconductor quantum dot in a microcavity, driven by pulsed excitation, emits exactly one photon per pulse. This turned the artificial atom into a triggered source of quantum light that can be built into a chip. Senellart then solved the long-standing problem of extraction and coherence. By deterministically positioning dots in micropillar cavities and exciting them resonantly, she produced single photons that are bright, pure and indistinguishable, surpassing heralded parametric sources. Together these advances turned a laboratory curiosity into a technology others depend on. Quantum-dot sources now drive boson-sampling and photonic quantum-computing experiments, quantum-key-distribution links and entanglement networks, and they are sold commercially. This work founded solid-state quantum photonics and made deterministic quantum light a reliable tool for physics.
